value.rationale: The two natural complexities of the same dynamical model quantify typical orbit branching versus histories accessible only through rare environmental realizations; the annealed interval extends beyond the typical rotation interval, and the two spectra are strictly separated at every shared nonmodal rate. Exact positive endpoint typical entropies, strict separation and bias-independent quadratic curvature give a complete natural classification that is not encoded in the motivating paper’s interval and unrestricted entropy; finite counting is linked to genuine branch trajectories by a uniform lift-error bound. Although related to standard symbolic pressure techniques, the model-specific quantitative contrast is motivated and potentially useful for distinguishing random orbit-selection from count complexity.
